headline: 布莉姬絲新專輯回歸
context: 美國創作歌手菲比．布莉姬絲（Phoebe Bridgers）睽違六年推出新專輯《Lost Weekend》，加入電子元素與不安的音效設計，唱出一種抽離、疏離的情緒——上一張個人專輯，還是疫情高峰期發行的。同一天，Prime Video新劇《Sterling Point》把背景設在加拿大小島，意外地引人入勝；倫敦南岸中心也把童書《Dog Man》搬上舞台，演成音樂劇。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: (Dead Oceans) After sweeping the Grammys and being scrutinised by the press, Bridgers deploys electronics and unsettling sound design to brilliantly evoke emotional turmoil The last time Phoebe Bridgers put out a solo album was six years ago, at the height of the Covid pandemic: Punisher not only ended 2020 near the top of many critics’ best-of lists, it made the UK Top 10 and sold half a million copies in the US. The intervening period has proved just as commercially triumphant. With the release of their debut album The Record, Boygenius – the band she had formed with Lucy Dacus and Julien Baker – went from a kind of supergroup for Pitchfork readers to a genuine mainstream phenomenon: the album won three Grammys. Another win, for Bridgers’ collaboration with SZA, Ghost in the Machine, meant Bridgers left the 2024 ceremony the night’s biggest winner. Other pop stars called on her services: she sang on Taylor Swift’s re-recorded version of Red (and supported on the Eras tour), Lorde’s Solar Power and on Paul McCartney’s McCartney III Imagined. But to judge by Lost Weekend’s opening track, all was not well. The Outside depicts the singer crowd-surfing at a gig in Ohio – “they never let me hit the ground, way beyond the barricade” – and ending a song with her fist triumphantly raised. Then it adds a qualifier. “But I was on the outside, watching,” she sings, the sense of dislocation heightened by the fact that her voice is smothered by a vocoder, and the musical accompaniment – a sweet fingerpicked acoustic guitar figure – keeps vanishing into an ambient backing that sounds like static. sources.title: Phoebe Bridgers: Lost Weekend review – long-awaited return is a thrilling, daring study in dislocation

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Southbank Centre, London A part-canine cop, a villainous cat and a psychokinetic butterflyfish burst into song as the wildly popular children’s books are adapted for the stage Perhaps, if you don’t have a child in primary school, you will be blissfully unaware of Dog Man, Dav Pilkey’s series of graphic novels about a cop who – after a terrible injury – has his dog’s head sewn on to his own body, thereby creating a crime-fighting canine/human crossbreed. But if you’ve been swept up by the phenomenon – and Dog Man is a phenomenon, selling more than 70m copies in the decade since the first book was published – then you will know that this mutt has some serious star power: there’s a Dog Man film , video game, board game … and now a musical, arriving in the UK after off-Broadway success. The Dog Man books are chaotic, hilarious and full of pathos, but writer/lyricist Kevin Del Aguila and composer Brad Alexander’s show leans largely on the former. There’s slapstick humour and jokes about butt-sniffing. When Dog Man is asked how his day is going, he replies: “Ruff!” It’s aimed at the younger end of Pilkey’s readership, which is confusing as there are also Dickens references. Continue reading...
sources.title: Dog Man: The Musical review – Dav Pilkey’s megastar mutt sniffs out the spotlight in a barking show

threads_text:
美國創作歌手菲比．布莉姬絲（Phoebe Bridgers）睽違六年推出新專輯《Lost Weekend》，這次她加入電子元素與不安的音效設計，唱出一種抽離、疏離的情緒——上一張個人專輯，還是疫情高峰期發行的。同一天，Prime Video新劇《Sterling Point》把背景設在加拿大一座小島，本來被認為是老套的青春劇，卻意外地引人入勝。倫敦南岸中心，也把暢銷童書《Dog Man》搬上舞台，改編成一齣音樂劇。

本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 8 月 5 日發佈的報導。
voice_text: 美國創作歌手菲比．布莉姬絲，睽違六年推出新專輯《Lost Weekend》。她這次加入了電子元素和有點不安的音效設計，唱出一種疏離、幾乎讓人抽離現場的情緒——上一張個人專輯，還是在疫情高峰期發行的。同一天，Prime Video的新劇《Sterling Point》，把背景設在加拿大一座小島，本來以為只是普通的青少年劇，結果意外地引人入勝。倫敦南岸中心，也把暢銷童書《Dog Man》搬上舞台，演成一齣音樂劇。
